Load a Timestral model

Source: R/safetensors.R
timestral_load.Rd

Load a Timestral model from the official Mistral AI checkpoint, another Hugging Face Hub repository, or a local checkpoint directory.

Usage

timestral_load(
  model = "5M",
  max_context = NULL,
  per_shot_horizon_patches = 32L,
  quantile_real_cap_k = 10000,
  extreme_value_threshold = 1e+30,
  revision = NULL,
  cache_dir = tools::R_user_dir("timestralR", "cache"),
  local_files_only = FALSE,
  token = Sys.getenv("HF_TOKEN", ""),
  backend = c("native", "R")
)

Arguments

model

a size ("5M", "28M", "123M", "209M") to download/cache, a local directory holding config.json and model.safetensors, or a Hugging Face repository ID ("owner/name") to download/cache. A local directory takes precedence over a repository ID of the same name.

max_context

context cap in steps; NULL (default) uses the trained context length from the checkpoint, as in the Python package

per_shot_horizon_patches

patches decoded per block (capped at the trained block size)

quantile_real_cap_k

clamp forecasts to the observed context range plus/minus this multiple of the last patch scale; 0 disables

extreme_value_threshold

fed-back medians at or above this magnitude become 0

revision

Hub revision when model is a size or repository ID; see timestral_download(). The default NULL uses the pinned, hash-verified upstream commit for an official size and "main" otherwise.

cache_dir

checkpoint cache directory for downloaded checkpoints

local_files_only

only read from the cache, never download

token

Hugging Face access token for private or gated repositories; defaults to the HF_TOKEN environment variable

backend

"native" (default) uses the compiled RcppEigen implementation of the transformer block; "R" uses the pure-R reference implementation. Results are identical up to floating-point order.

Value

A timestral_model object.

Examples

## A tiny random-weight checkpoint ships with the package, so this runs
## offline; its forecasts are meaningless. Use a size such as "5M" or
## "28M" (downloaded once) for real forecasts.
m <- timestral_load(system.file("extdata", "tiny", package = "timestralR"))
fc <- timestral_forecast(m, AirPassengers, h = 24)
plot(fc)

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
m <- timestral_load("5M")
m <- timestral_load("mistralai/Timestral-28M")
} # }
